provenance: Authored by the project assistant on 2026-11-18 for prototype diagnostics. No natural recordings or independent annotator review.

labels.on_topic: Advances or questions the stated motion, including relevant examples and context-dependent follow-ups.
labels.off_topic: Discusses a separate subject with no stated connection to the motion.
labels.unclear: Acknowledgement or insufficient standalone content to judge relevance.

sessions.topic: Should schools require students to wear uniforms?
turns: School uniforms could reduce pressure to buy fashionable clothes.
Parents might spend more if only one shop sells the required school clothing.
Did you watch the football match last night?
The goalkeeper saved two penalties and the crowd went wild.
My cousin bought tickets for the next league game.
We should return to whether uniforms actually help students learn.
Some children need an exemption for religious or sensory reasons.
Yes, the uniform policy should include reasonable exemptions.

sessions.topic: Should the city make public bus travel free?
turns: Free bus fares could encourage commuters to leave their cars at home.
The city could use parking revenue to fund public transport.
I bought a new coffee grinder this weekend.
But even a free bus is unattractive if it arrives late.
More frequent services may matter more than abolishing fares.
Students with low incomes could receive discounted transit passes instead.
We should compare the cost of fare subsidies with improving bus frequency.

sessions.topic: Should mobile phones be banned during classroom lessons?
turns: Phones interrupt classroom lessons when notifications distract students.
A phone can also be a useful classroom dictionary.
My sister is planning a beach holiday in December.
She should book the hotel before the rooms sell out.
We should compare classroom phone restrictions with supervised educational use.
Teachers could permit devices only for a specific activity.
It would require clear classroom rules and consistent enforcement.

sessions.topic: Should office employees be allowed to work from home?
turns: Working from home removes the daily commute for many office staff.
Some employees lack a quiet workspace or reliable internet at home.
Companies might provide equipment and allow optional office days.
A colleague in another firm says scheduled video calls help remote collaboration.
Too many meetings can reduce productive work regardless of location.
A hybrid schedule could balance flexibility and coordination.
We should assess results rather than hours spent sitting in the office.

sessions.topic: Should public universities stop charging tuition fees?
turns: Removing university tuition could let more low-income students earn a degree.
Taxpayers would have to replace the income universities receive from tuition.
My new headphones have much better noise cancellation.
They were expensive, but the sound quality is excellent.
Let's return to whether free university education is fair to taxpayers.
Graduates often earn more, so targeted grants may be fairer than universal free tuition.
Students still need support for rent and food even when tuition is covered.

sessions.topic: Should the country build more nuclear power stations?
turns: Nuclear power can supply electricity when wind and solar generation fall.
New reactors take years to construct and can exceed their budgets.
Construction delays can postpone the expected electricity supply for several years.
I tried making sourdough bread yesterday.
We also have to account for radioactive waste storage when comparing power sources.
A nuclear expansion plan needs long-term waste management and independent inspection.
The decision should compare nuclear reliability, cost and safety with other low-carbon electricity.

sessions.topic: Should the city replace some car lanes with protected bicycle lanes?
turns: Protected bicycle lanes could make cycling safer for people travelling across the city.
Removing a car lane may increase congestion before drivers change their habits.
We could measure traffic around a temporary cycle lane before building a permanent one.
My cat refuses to eat the new food I bought.
Have you tried mixing it with the old food?
No, I will try that tonight and ask the vet tomorrow.
For the bicycle lane proposal, delivery drivers still need places to unload.
Loading bays could be placed beside the protected cycle route.
Did the bakery finally reopen on your street?
It did, and the pastries sold out before noon.
We should finish by deciding which streets are suitable for the bicycle lanes.

sessions.topic: Should primary schools limit the amount of homework?
turns: Shorter homework assignments would leave children time to sleep and play.
Children still need some practice reading and doing arithmetic outside class.
Teachers could set a short daily reading task instead of several worksheets.
Some parents cannot help with schoolwork after a long work shift.
A school library session could offer support before children go home.
The school would need transport arrangements if the homework club runs late.
A limit should vary with the child's age and learning needs.
